headerDisplay:
Homebridge plugin for Philips air purifiers and humidifiers.

**Before this plugin can talk to any device**, the [`aioairctrl`](https://pypi.org/project/aioairctrl/) command-line tool must be installed **for the user that runs Homebridge** — this plugin runs it to speak the encrypted protocol the purifiers use. It is not installed automatically:

```
pipx install aioairctrl
```

Then check it works for the Homebridge user: `sudo -u homebridge aioairctrl --help`. If it only runs for another user, or lives outside that user's PATH (pipx installs to `~/.local/bin`, which services often do not search), run `which aioairctrl` and put the full path into **aioairctrl Path** below.

The plugin checks this at startup and explains what to fix in the Homebridge log if it cannot run the command.

aioairctrlPath.title: aioairctrl Path
aioairctrlPath.description: Only needed if aioairctrl is not on the PATH of the user running Homebridge. Run 'which aioairctrl' as that user and paste the full path here, e.g. /home/pi/.local/bin/aioairctrl. Leave empty to look it up on the PATH.

debug.title: Debug Log
debug.description: Logs every device status and command. Switch this on before reporting a problem, and off again afterwards — it is very noisy.

warn.title: Warn Log
warn.description: Reports problems the plugin recovered from, such as a lost command or a device that stopped responding. Unchecking this hides those reports; it does not stop them happening.

error.title: Error Log
error.description: Reports the underlying error behind a problem. Unchecking this hides the detail that usually says what to fix. Faults that stop the plugin working at all are always reported.

extendedError.title: Extended Error Log
extendedError.description: Includes the full stack trace with each error. Useful when reporting an issue.

condition.functionBody: try { return model.error } catch(e){ return false }

active.title: Active
active.description: If enabled, the device will be exposed to HomeKit.

name.title: Name
name.description: Your own label for this device in the Home app. It does not tell the plugin what the device is; the Model field does that.

manufacturer.title: Manufacturer
manufacturer.description: Shown in the Home app. Cosmetic only.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model ID printed on your device. Ignore any /11 or /31 suffix. It selects the commands the plugin sends, so a missing or wrong model is the usual reason the Home app controls do nothing. Suggested models are tested; anything else uses a default mapping that may not fit.

serialNumber.title: Serial Number
serialNumber.description: Shown in the Home app. Cosmetic only.

host.title: Host Address
host.description: IP address or hostname of your device. Give it a fixed address first, usually a DHCP reservation on your router: if the address changes, the plugin can no longer reach the device.

refreshInterval.title: Refresh Interval
refreshInterval.description: Seconds after a reading before the plugin asks the device for another one, by re-subscribing. Raise it if your device reports on its own often enough; set it to 0 to switch the refresh off and rely entirely on the device. Values below 15 are treated as 15.

humidifier.title: Humidifier
humidifier.description: Expose a separate humidifier accessory to HomeKit.

light.title: Light
light.description: Expose device lights as lightbulbs to HomeKit.

temperature.title: Temperature sensor
temperature.description: Expose device temperature as temperature sensor to HomeKit.

humidity.title: Humidity sensor
humidity.description: Expose device humidity as humidity sensor to HomeKit.

sleepSpeed.title: Sleep Speed
sleepSpeed.description: Adds a 'sleep' step below the lowest fan speed. Ignored for models with their own speed mapping (pick your model above and the plugin uses the right speeds automatically).

carbonFilter.title: Active Carbon Filter
carbonFilter.description: Expose active carbon filter status to HomeKit.

hepaFilter.title: HEPA Filter
hepaFilter.description: Expose HEPA/NanoProtect filter status to HomeKit.
